function.name: search_code
function.description: Search the codebase for a pattern using ripgrep. Returns matched lines with a couple lines of context, not full files.

file_type.description: Restrict to a file type, e.g. go, py, js

path.description: Directory or file to search under (default: project root)

pattern.description: Regex or literal pattern to search for

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a line range from a file. Files over 400 lines require start_line/end_line — search first to find the range you need.

path.description: File path, relative to project root

function.name: read_pdf
function.description: Extract the text of a PDF (slides, papers, manuals), a page range at a time, with --- page N --- markers. Default: 10 pages from first_page.

path.description: PDF path, relative to the project or absolute in a directory the user added

function.name: list_directory
function.description: List a directory as an indented tree, up to a given depth. Skips .git, node_modules, vendor, and build output.

depth.description: How many levels deep to recurse (default: 2)

path.description: Directory to list (default: project root)

function.name: run_command
function.description: Run an allowlisted, read-only binary directly (no shell). args is always an array of separate arguments, never one shell string.

args.description: Arguments as separate array entries, e.g. ["log", "--oneline", "-5"]

binary.description: Bare binary name, e.g. git, wc, find

function.name: run_program
function.description: Build, compile, test or run code: make, cmake, gcc, g++, clang, mpicc, mpirun, go, cargo, python3, node, npm... or a program the project built ("./build/app"). Binary plus an args array, no shell: feed a file as input with stdin, save the output with stdout (then diff it). For pipes, use binary bash with args ["-c", "..."] — always asked. The user approves each run. Prefer run_tests / build_check when they fit.

binary.description: Program: a bare name (make, gcc, mpirun) or a relative path inside the project (./fox)

dir.description: Working directory inside the project (default: project root), e.g. "build"

stdin.description: Project file to feed as the program's input, like < file, e.g. "tests/input/input6"

stdout.description: Project file to write the program's output to, like > file, e.g. "build/out6.txt"

function.name: edit_file
function.description: Replace an exact string in a file. Read the file first. old_string must match exactly once, whitespace included — add surrounding lines to make it unique, or set replace_all. Prefer this over write_file for changes to existing files.

old_string.description: Exact text to replace, copied from read_file

path.description: File path, relative to project root

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite one you have already read. Parent directories are created. Use edit_file for partial changes.

path.description: File path, relative to project root

function.name: web_search
function.description: Search the web for information not in this codebase — library docs, error messages, current facts. Starts a local search service on first use; returns a short list of title/url/snippet results, not full pages.

count.description: Number of results to return (default 5, max 10)

topic.description: general: web pages and docs (default); code: Stack Overflow and GitHub; science: papers (arXiv, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex)

function.name: count_lines
function.description: Count lines of code across the project (or a subdirectory) in one call — total, plus a breakdown by top-level directory.

path.description: Directory to count under (default: project root)

function.name: list_languages
function.description: Break the project down by file extension — file and line counts per language, ranked by lines.

path.description: Directory to scan (default: project root)

function.name: find_files
function.description: Find files by name using a glob pattern (e.g. "*.go", "*_test.go") — a name-only complement to search_code's content search.

path.description: Directory to search under (default: project root)

pattern.description: Glob matched against each file's base name

function.name: file_stat
function.description: Get a file's size, line count, and modification time without reading its content — cheaper than read_file for deciding what to read.

path.description: File path, relative to project root

function.name: find_todo_fixme
function.description: Find TODO/FIXME/XXX comment markers in the codebase.

path.description: Directory or file to search under (default: project root)

function.name: env_info
function.description: Report the toolchain available: Go version, OS/arch, and whether git/ripgrep/docker are installed.

function.name: project_manifest
function.description: Get an orientation snapshot of the project: directory tree plus the first README/manifest file found. Useful for "what kind of project is this" mid-conversation.

function.name: find_definition
function.description: Find where a function, type, or variable is defined — a deterministic index lookup, not a guess.

from_file.description: File you're currently looking at, to rank same-file/same-dir matches first

function.name: list_symbols
function.description: Fuzzy-search every known symbol name in the project (functions, types, variables, ...).

query.description: Substring to match against symbol names (empty lists everything, capped)

function.name: outline_file
function.description: List a file's known symbols without reading its content — a cheap first look at a large file before deciding what range to read.

path.description: File path, relative to project root

function.name: find_references
function.description: Find where an identifier is USED (not where it's defined — see find_definition), word-boundary matched.

path.description: Directory or file to search under (default: project root)

function.name: git_log
function.description: Get structured commit history (hash, author, date, subject) for the project or one path.

path.description: Limit history to this path (default: whole repo)

function.name: git_blame
function.description: Get per-line author/date attribution for a line range in a file.

path.description: File path, relative to project root

function.name: git_diff
function.description: Diff between two refs (default: HEAD vs. the working tree) for a path or the whole repo.

path.description: Limit the diff to this path (default: whole repo)

function.name: git_show
function.description: Get one commit's full diff and message by hash.

function.name: working_tree_diff
function.description: Show uncommitted changes only — what you've edited but not committed, plus untracked files.

path.description: Limit to this path (default: whole repo)

function.name: grep_history
function.description: Find when a piece of text was introduced or removed in git history (a "pickaxe" search).

path.description: Limit to this path (default: whole repo)

term.description: Text to search for across commit history

function.name: code_owners
function.description: Approximate who owns a path, by commit count per author — a heuristic, not an authoritative CODEOWNERS lookup.

path.description: Path to check (default: whole repo)

function.name: commit_stats
function.description: Rank files by how often they've changed — a churn/hotspot signal for what's worth extra scrutiny.

path.description: Limit to this path (default: whole repo)

function.name: run_tests
function.description: Run the project's test command (detected from Makefile, go.mod, Cargo.toml, package.json, or Python config; or user-configured). Reports pass/fail, a failure summary, and the end of the output.

args.description: Extra arguments replacing the default target, e.g. ["./internal/tools", "-run", "TestX"] or ["-k", "parser"]

function.name: build_check
function.description: Run the project's build or type-check command and report pass/fail plus errors. Run it after editing code.

args.description: Extra arguments replacing the default target, e.g. ["./cmd/..."]

function.name: lint_check
function.description: Run the project's linter; reports available:false if the project has none.

args.description: Extra arguments replacing the default target

function.name: list_dependencies
function.description: List the project's declared dependencies, parsed from whichever manifest exists (go.mod, package.json, requirements.txt, Cargo.toml, pyproject.toml).

function.name: module_graph
function.description: Show which of this Go module's own packages import which — internal architecture, not the full stdlib/third-party dependency closure.

function.name: read_doc_comment
function.description: Get just a symbol's doc comment, without reading the whole file it's defined in.

from_file.description: File you're currently looking at, to disambiguate a common name

function.name: find_callers
function.description: Find syntactic call sites of a Go function/method name — matched by identifier text, not type-checked, so treat results as leads, not certainties.

name.description: Function or method name to find call sites of

function.name: find_dead_code
function.description: Find exported Go functions/methods with no syntactic call sites anywhere in the project — a possibly-unused signal, not proof; can false-positive, notably on exported struct fields (ctags can't distinguish them from methods).

path.description: Limit the scan to this file/directory prefix

function.name: impact_analysis
function.description: Find functions that transitively call a given Go function, up to a bounded depth — what might need re-checking if it changes.

depth.description: How many call levels out to trace (default 2, max 3)

name.description: Function or method name to analyze

function.name: semantic_search
function.description: Keyword/term-frequency relevance search across the codebase — NOT true embedding-based semantic search. Useful when you don't know the exact text to grep for; prefer search_code when you do.

count.description: Number of results to return (default 5, max 15)

query.description: Natural-language description of what you're looking for

function.name: memory_save
function.description: Save a durable fact for future sessions: user preferences, project conventions, decisions and their reasons. Not for task progress (use the scratchpad). Overwrites a memory of the same name.

content.description: The fact, plus why it matters and how to apply it

description.description: One line — shown in the index every session

scope.description: project (this codebase, default) or user (every project)

function.name: memory_read
function.description: Read a memory listed in the index.

function.name: memory_delete
function.description: Delete a memory that's wrong or obsolete.

function.name: scratchpad_write
function.description: Write working notes to a scratch file outside the project: plans, findings, long reasoning, checklists. Keep only the file name in mind afterwards and re-read it when needed — this frees context for the work.

name.description: File name, e.g. plan or findings

function.name: scratchpad_read
function.description: Read a scratch file, or a line range of it.

function.name: scratchpad_list
function.description: List scratch files with their sizes.

function.name: request_access
function.description: Ask the user for read access to a directory outside the project (e.g. slides or docs in the parent folder). The user approves or declines; on approval, read tools accept absolute paths in it. Read-only: writes stay inside the project.

dir.description: Directory: absolute, ~/..., or relative to the project ("..")

reason.description: One line: why you need it

function.name: use_skill
function.description: Load a skill's instructions (see the skill index) before doing a task it covers. With file, read one of its supporting files instead.

file.description: Supporting file path, as listed by a previous use_skill

function.name: library_search
function.description: Search the user's reference library (books, official docs, language standards, RFCs, man pages) for passages on a technical question. Returns the best passages with title, file, page or line, and how to read more. Cite what you use as [Title, page N].

query.description: Keywords, e.g. "happens before channel close" or "epoll edge triggered"

topic.description: Optional: keep to the books of one topic (see library_topics), e.g. concurrency, sql, linear-algebra

function.name: library_topics
function.description: Show where the library covers a topic: book, chapters or pages, and what it's good for. With no topic, lists every topic.

topic.description: Topic name or part of it, e.g. memory, http, calculus
